correctness.rationale: Identity (1) partitions every J(n,2) edge by its unique shared label; identity (2) removes exactly the n-2 token edges corresponding to moving along the deleted base edge. Each local clique term is bounded by discrete concavity, and the odd handshake obstruction supplies the exact one-unit penalty for n=3 modulo 4; no external upper-bound theorem is required. All four modular red-graph constructions achieve that ceiling and avoid all deleted cut edges for orders other than five. For n=5, the handshake lemma eliminates score 19 and every full-optimum five-cycle loses exactly two deleted crossing edges; direct degree classification yields 32 ordered optima. The embedded verifier exhausts all cuts for orders three through six and checks all constructions through order one hundred.

value.rationale: An explicit and unexpectedly almost-perfect stability law under deletion of an (n-2)-edge matching in a well-studied Johnson graph, with one sharp exceptional order and a structural characterization of all optimum cuts. The obstruction is degree-balance versus endpoint synchrony, revealing why the known general inequality can be strict in the smallest nontrivial case. It is a natural perturbation of a published exact invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
